idiom_name: lambda/proc closing over the method's local variables; explicit class when the computation is a unit
implementation_notes: Proc objects are closures: they remember and can use the entire context in which they were created (ruby-doc), so steps defined with lambda (or ->) read and write the same locals without any class, and blocks passed to each/map are the same mechanism. Write the explicit class - named after the computation, with an initializer that captures the receiver and arguments and a compute method - when the algorithm must be tested, reused or documented as a unit. Do not confuse this with Ruby's Method objects (Object#method), which are first-class references bound to an existing method rather than a class created for one invocation.
pitfalls: Ruby's Method class (obj.method(:price)) is a bound reference to an existing method, not the Method Object pattern; describing a realization that way misleads readers.
Non-lambda procs treat return as returning from the enclosing method (and raise LocalJumpError if called after it returns); use lambda semantics for steps that must behave like methods.
Capture is by binding, so a proc created in a loop sees the loop variable's final value unless the value is passed in as a block parameter of a factory.
